sources: dossier=module-layout(Net position: 'lib/services is its own module requiring only lib/protocols'); doc=.golangci.yml:141-144; code=lib/services/go.mod:5-21
note: lib/services/go.mod currently requires github.com/rimsky-ai/rimsky-core (root) and lib/foundation in addition to lib/protocols, so the depguard comment's module-graph claim is factually false today; the depguard rule itself still functions as defense-in-depth. Fix: update the comment to state the module also requires root+foundation and that depguard is therefore the primary (not merely defense-in-depth) guard against a rimsky-internal import from lib/services.

sources: dossier=host-agent-proxy(Required behaviors: write-semantics envelope is intentionally canned/pure-transport; Conflicts RESOLVED 2026-07-14: executor+claim-producer remain the sanctioned late-bind surface, no-Unimplemented-stub promise stands for them); code=cmd/rimsky-host-agent-proxy/claim_producer_handler.go:42-53 (canned Capabilities, no SplitScope/ScopesConflict handlers, embeds UnimplementedClaimProducerServer)
note: The finding is half-refuted: the canned Capabilities response (full write-semantics envelope) is intentional per the dossier ('pure transport; any binding might realize any semantics'), not a bug. But claim-producer is a still-sanctioned late-bind protocol post-2026-07-14, and the handler advertises SupportsSplitScope:true while the SplitScope RPC falls through to codes.Unimplemented -- a real advertise/implement mismatch violating the still-live transparent-forwarder invariant. Fix: forward SplitScope (and ScopesConflict, or flip its advertised bit) to the spawned child; leave Capabilities canned as designed.

sources: dossier=host-agent-proxy(Conflicts, RESOLVED 2026-07-14, transcript tier: late-bind surface narrowed to executor+claim-producer; publisher/validation/data-processing are REJECTED loudly at registration/config, and 'the proxy's server-side handlers for the unreachable three protocols are trimmed per erase-completely'); code=cmd/rimsky-host-agent-proxy/data_processing_handler.go (full handler still registered in main.go), lib/control/controlapi/templates.go (no rejection of late-binding a data-processing-slot service)
note: The finding's literal remediation (forward ListVersions/ListPartitions/GetVersionSchema) is now superseded intent -- per the 2026-07-14 user ruling, data-processing must not be late-bindable at all. The code has NOT caught up to that ruling either: the handler is still fully registered (not trimmed) and there is no registration/config-time rejection of late-binding a data-processing service, so the gap remains, just relocated. Fix: trim dataProcessingHandler entirely and add a loud registration-time rejection for late-binding non-(executor|claim-producer) protocol slots, per the RESOLVED conflict.

sources: dossier=host-agent-proxy(Conflicts, RESOLVED 2026-07-14, transcript tier); code=cmd/rimsky-host-agent-proxy/publisher_handler.go (still registered, ListSubscriptions unimplemented), lib/control/controlapi/templates.go (no compose/late-bind protocol-kind rejection)
note: Same family as 84: publisher is no longer a sanctioned late-bind protocol per the 2026-07-14 ruling (executor+claim-producer only), so the fix is not 'forward ListSubscriptions' but 'trim publisherHandler and reject late-binding a publisher slot at registration/config,' which the code does not yet do.

sources: doc=.ok-planner/design/concepts/host-agent.md:29 (corrected: 'authentication is the user's api-key, supplied via RIMSKY_API_KEY or --api-key (there is no active-context config)'); dossier=host-agent(Net position: agent auth via RIMSKY_API_KEY/--api-key); code=cmd/rimsky/cli/agent.go:52-77
note: The design corpus has already been corrected by the remediation pass to explicitly say there is NO active-context config for the agent -- the exact opposite of what the finding's cited invariant said. Current code (LoadConfigFromEnv + --api-key/--proxy flags, no active-context read) now matches the corrected doc and the dossier exactly. The doc was the stale side and has already been fixed; the finding is refuted against current sources.

sources: dossier=host-agent(Required behaviors: 'status verb truthfully reports connection state, proxy endpoint, and spawned children'); doc=.ok-planner/design/stories/host-agent-control-plane.md Acceptance ('the list of currently-spawned children (per run-scope, per binding)'); code=cmd/rimsky/cli/agent.go:294 statusSnapshot{Connected,Proxy,Since}, lib/runtime/hostagent/run.go:219 statusSnapshot (no children field), run.go:57 children map never written to status
note: Still true at dev tip: statusSnapshot carries only Connected/Proxy/Since; the live children map (run.go:58) is never serialized to the status file, so `rimsky agent status` cannot report spawned children as the story's acceptance requires. Fix: add a children (run-scope/binding) field to statusSnapshot and populate it from the agent's live children map when writing the status file.

sources: dossier=frame(Net position: 'A frame is, by product definition, one complete run of the graph...'); code=cmd/rimsky/cli/compose/wait.go:116,146-153, cmd/rimsky/cli/compose/progress.go:75,168
note: Confirmed still present: classifyInstanceOutcome returns len(nodes) as its second value, which wait.go:116 hands to InstanceTerminal(...frames int), printed/JSON-keyed as 'frames'. 'Frame' is a distinct, load-bearing concept (one cascade run) per the frame dossier and concept doc; labeling node count as frames is a clear vocabulary bug with no countervailing intent. Fix: rename the return value/field to node count (e.g. nodes) and update progress.go's format string and JSON key plus wait_test.go's assertions.

sources: dossier=parked-state(ParkReason closed 2-value enum today: await_callback, snooze; RESOLVED 2026-07-14 retires await_callback but not yet landed in code); code=lib/foundation/spec/parked_reason.go:12-18 (still {await_callback, snooze}), cmd/rimsky/cli/parked.go:21
note: Confirmed: the closed ParkReason enum today is {await_callback, snooze}; 'awaiting_human' is neither. Fix: change the CLI help example to 'snooze' (or 'await_callback'). Note the dossier's 2026-07-14 ruling retires await_callback entirely -- not yet implemented in code -- so once that lands the only valid example will be 'snooze'; either fix is correct for the code as it stands today.

sources: dossier=lifecycle-subscriber(Net position: 'Lifecycle is universal across peer kinds (claim-producer, executor, publisher, sensor)...'; Corrections: peersReferencedBySpec fix 2026-06-19 08d65bfe transcript, 'ruled clearly a bug'); code=lib/control/config/claim_producers.go:613 DialLifecycleSubscribers(ctx, stores, execs) -- no publishers param; call sites controlapi.go:129, supervisor.go:142
note: The 2026-06-19 fix only repaired the fan-out CANDIDATE set (peersReferencedBySpec now walks spec.Publishers); the dial/registration step (DialLifecycleSubscribers) was never extended to dial publishers, so a publisher declaring lifecycle_subscriber still validates at registration, is enumerated as a fan-out candidate, but is never in the lifecycle registry and is silently skipped as not_subscribed at fan-out time. Fix: extend DialLifecycleSubscribers to also dial publishers advertising lifecycle_subscriber (needs a publishers config param threaded through both call sites).

sources: dossier=frame(Required behaviors: 'The held-frames diagnostic surfaces frames held by parked nodes (scoped to phase=parked)' 2026-06-17 b95ff4a7 transcript); doc=.ok-planner/design/concepts/frame.md Held-frames section (corrected: 'the held-frames diagnostics endpoint... surfaces frames held by a parked node-run; held-claim holds are not reported there... every in-flight state holds the frame open for frame-end purposes, but the held-frames diagnostic reports only the parked subset'); code=lib/control/controlapi/admin_diagnostics.go:79-83 handleAdminHeldFrames (parked-only, by design)
note: The design corpus has already been corrected to explicitly document that the held-frames diagnostic intentionally reports only the parked subset of held frames, not held-claim (state='held') holds -- exactly matching current code, and directly corroborated by the frame intent dossier's transcript-tier ruling. The finding's premise (that omitting held-state runs is a bug) is refuted. Adjacent nit not part of this finding's scope: actions.go:384's route description ('List frames held by holding-subgraph claims') still overclaims relative to the corrected doc and could use a wording fix, but that is a separate, much smaller issue than what was alleged here.

sources: dossier=asset(Net position: 'An asset is a documented compound... a claim against a DataProcessing-capable producer with lifetime: durable'); doc=.ok-planner/design/concepts/asset.md Invariants ('The producer MUST advertise the data-processing capability... not surfaced as an asset'); code=lib/control/controlapi/assets.go:183-227 resolveAsset (no capability check), :270 handleGetAsset, :108 handleListAssets (has the check via buildDataProcessingPredicate)
note: Still true at dev tip: resolveAsset backs GET /instances/{id}/assets/{alias} with no data-processing capability check, while handleListAssets applies buildDataProcessingPredicate -- an alias absent from LIST is still returned by GET, contradicting the asset compound definition both the dossier and the concept doc agree on. Fix: apply the same data-processing capability check inside resolveAsset (or at its GET/history/delete call sites) as handleListAssets already does.

sources: dossier=asset(Net position, same as 96); doc=.ok-planner/design/concepts/asset.md Invariants; code=lib/control/controlapi/assets.go:183-227 resolveAsset used by handleGetAsset:287, handleAssetMaterializationHistory:411, handleDeleteAsset:451
note: Same underlying gap as 96 (resolveAsset lacks the data-processing capability check), affecting detail, materialization-history, and delete in addition to GET. One fix (gating resolveAsset itself) closes both 96 and 97.

sources: dossier=asset(Required behaviors: 'DELETE /instances/{id}/assets/{alias} calls ClaimProducer.Release; the producer GCs the durable data per its own policy'); doc=.ok-planner/design/concepts/asset.md:24 ('The asset-delete endpoint releases the claim handle via the producer's release verb'); code=lib/control/controlapi/assets.go:507-516
note: Confirmed still present: Release is called only when deps.ClaimProducers != nil AND the producer is registered; every negative branch falls straight through to DeleteResolved with no error or log, deleting rimsky's ledger row while the producer-side durable resource is never released -- a silent leak against the delete contract both the dossier and the doc state as mandatory. Fix: fail the delete (don't proceed to DeleteResolved) when the producer can't be reached to Release, rather than silently skipping.

sources: dossier=asset(Net position, MUST-advertise definition); doc=.ok-planner/design/concepts/asset.md:22 ('The producer MUST advertise the data-processing capability'); code=lib/control/controlapi/assets.go:158-172 buildDataProcessingPredicate
note: Confirmed still present: nil ClaimProducers registry, an unregistered producer, or a Capabilities() error all cause buildDataProcessingPredicate to return true (list-as-asset) -- fail-open against the doc's unconditional MUST. Same family as 96/97/99; a quality gap on the one call site (handleListAssets) that does have the check.

sources: doc=.ok-planner/design/concepts/anonymous-mode.md Invariants ('Operators cannot stay in anonymous mode after a key exists without explicitly revoking it'); dossier=anonymous-mode(Required behaviors: revoke-last-key guard, artifact tier); code=lib/foundation/persistence/postgres/api_keys.go:124-130 ActiveCount (excludes expired/past-revoke_at rows), lib/control/controlapi/auth_handlers.go:56-159 handleCreateKey (no last-key/past-expiry guard), :199-243 force_leave_anonymous guard (checked only at revoke time)
note: Confirmed still present: the explicit revoke path is guarded (force_leave_anonymous), but ActiveCount's predicate flips to zero the instant the sole active key's expires_at or rotation-grace revoke_at lapses, with no guard on those paths -- the deployment silently re-enters all-admin anonymous mode without any explicit operator action, contradicting the doc's unconditional invariant. Fix: refuse (or WARN-and-require-force) a create/rotate that would leave zero non-expiring active keys, or otherwise close the expiry/grace re-entry path.

sources: dossier=breakpoint(Net position: 'overflow_policy... auto_resume_after_ttl (either)' -- legal for both pause and notify_only modes); doc=.ok-planner/design/concepts/breakpoint.md:31 ('Notify-only mode combined with a blocking overflow policy is rejected at registration'); code=lib/control/controlapi/breakpoints.go:446-448 resolveOverflowPolicy (rejects only notify_only+block_dispatch), lib/runtime/breakpoint_eval.go:187-207 handleOverflow (treats OverflowBlockDispatch and OverflowAutoResumeAfterTTL identically -- both fall into the same busy-poll blocking branch)
note: The dossier (higher authority than the concept doc) explicitly ratifies notify_only+auto_resume_after_ttl as a legal combination, so the finding's literal remediation (reject that combination at registration) is wrong direction. But the underlying complaint is real: handleOverflow currently blocks the calling goroutine identically for BlockDispatch and AutoResumeAfterTTL, so a notify_only breakpoint with auto_resume_after_ttl genuinely blocks the runner once the 100-hit cap is reached -- violating the doc's non-blocking-notify_only invariant at the runtime level, not the registration level. Fix: make AutoResumeAfterTTL's overflow handling non-blocking for notify_only mode (or otherwise differentiate it from BlockDispatch) in handleOverflow, leaving resolveOverflowPolicy's registration check as-is.

sources: doc=.ok-planner/design/concepts/frame.md Boundaries ('Owns: ...the root-RunScope pointer (created at frame start)'), concepts/run-scope.md:15,37; code=lib/control/controlapi/frames.go:27-38 frameItem (no RootRunScopeID field), lib/foundation/persistence/frames.go:36 FrameRow.RootRunScopeID
note: Confirmed still present: FrameRow.RootRunScopeID is selected by every observability query but frameItem omits it, so the frames operator surface gives no way to correlate a frame to its RunScope tree, even though the frame concept doc names the root-RunScope pointer as an owned, first-class frame property. Fix: add root_run_scope_id to frameItem and toFrameItem.

sources: dossier=transition-reason(Net position: 'instance_killed is a state-machine-validation-only reason... with exactly running->failed and parked->failed arms', 2026-05-28 artifact, predates the held state and the 2026-06-20 seven-state redesign); doc=.ok-planner/design/concepts/transition-reason.md ('accepted... only from... running, parked... rejects it from... fresh, stale'); doc=.ok-planner/design/concepts/node-run.md:59-61 (instance_killed legal from held, plus pending/stale/running/parked per the transition table); code=lib/foundation/cascade/state.go:68-121 NextState (accepts instance_killed from all five in-flight states: pending, stale, running, held, parked)
note: Genuine doc-vs-doc conflict, already flagged internally by finding 948: transition-reason.md and the transition-reason dossier's 2026-05-28 ruling say instance_killed is legal only from running/parked, but node-run.md and the current code agree on all five in-flight states. The dossier's narrow ruling predates both the held state's introduction and the 2026-06-20 seven-state redesign, so it's unclear whether it was ever revisited for the new states. Separately, the operator-facing killStates set at instances.go:657 ({running,parked,held}) is itself consistent with the 'leave pending/stale inert' intent regardless of which side wins, since it never force-fails pending/stale runs. Question for a human: should transition-reason.md be widened to match node-run.md/code (5 in-flight states), or should NextState/node-run.md be narrowed to running/parked/held only, given the 2026-05-28 ruling never explicitly addressed the post-redesign held state?

sources: doc=.ok-planner/design/concepts/lineage-record.md:18 ('Does NOT own: the projection storage or query surface (lives in concept:lineage)'), concepts/lineage.md:17 ('Owns: ...the operator-facing lineage query surface'); code=lib/control/controlapi/lineage.go:5 (`// @concept: lineage-record`)
note: Confirmed: lineage.go implements the operator-facing lineage query handlers, which lineage-record.md explicitly disowns in favor of lineage.md, which explicitly owns the query surface. The citation resolves (so citation_resolution lint stays green) but points at the wrong boundary doc. Fix: change the file-level annotation to `// @concept: lineage`.

sources: doc=.ok-planner/design/decisions/idempotency-key-header-universal.md ('A mandatory idempotency-key header on the universal message-send endpoint... Replay-safe by construction'); dossier=message(Required behaviors: 'Mandatory Idempotency-Key'); dossier=control-api(Net position: MCP transport parity -- 'invoking a tool fires the same auth gate, produces the same state, returns the same response'); code=lib/control/controlapi/mcp_route.go:88 message_send inputSchema (no idempotency_key field), lib/control/controlapi/mcp/catalog.go:127 (mints a fresh random 'mcp-'+uuid per call)
note: Confirmed still present: message_send's MCP schema exposes only id/type/payload/sender/publisher_subscription_id and the catalog synthesizes a fresh random Idempotency-Key on every POST, so an MCP client retry after a timeout double-sends the message -- exactly the scenario the mandatory header exists to prevent, and a violation of the documented MCP/HTTP transport-parity invariant. Fix: add an idempotency_key argument to the message_send tool schema and thread it through to the Idempotency-Key header, falling back to a random key only when the caller omits it.

sources: doc=.ok-planner/design/decisions/message-sender-kind-discriminator.md ('The orthogonal sender-subject identity field carries the actor identity (api-key id, publisher subscription, or the anonymous sentinel...)'); dossier=message(Conflicts, RESOLVED 2026-07-14: 'dedups per (instance, sender_kind, sender, sender_subject, idempotency_key): publishers by name...' -- silent on subscription-level granularity, does not contradict the decision doc); code=lib/control/controlapi/messages.go:195 (`sender = row.PublisherName; senderSubject = ""`)
note: The decision doc explicitly names 'publisher subscription' as one of the three things sender_subject is supposed to carry, but the publisher send path hardcodes senderSubject to empty string, so two live subscriptions of the same publisher name on one instance (or a re-mounted subscription) share a dedup namespace and the subscription id is not recorded on the dedup row at all. The 2026-07-14 dossier ruling describes dedup as 'publishers by name' but doesn't address subscription-level granularity, so it doesn't retract the decision doc's more specific claim. Fix: set senderSubject to the publisher-subscription id (row.ID.String()) on the publisher send path.

sources: dossier=tag(Net position/Required behaviors: 'the control-api rejects compose:-prefixed creates from foreign clients with 400', 2026-06-06 comprehensive-gap-closure); dossier=control-api(Net position: 'control-api rejects foreign compose:-prefixed creates with 400', same 2026-06-06 session); doc=.ok-planner/design/concepts/tag.md:26 ('tag-create rejects a compose:-prefixed name unless the request originates from the privileged compose path'); code=lib/control/controlapi/tags.go:65 handleCreateTag (has the check), :143 handleMoveTag / :193 handleDeleteTag (no check)
note: Both intent dossiers (tag and control-api, independently distilled but tracing to the same 2026-06-06 session) and tag.md consistently scope the server-enforced compose-prefix reservation to CREATE only. Ordinary move/delete of an existing compose:-tagged tag by a caller holding the normal tag:set/tag:delete permission grant is not described anywhere as requiring an additional compose-origin check -- normal permission scoping governs it like any other tag. The finding's premise (that move/delete must also gate on compose-origin) is refuted by the create-only reading three independent artifacts agree on. Note: control-api.md:27's broader phrasing ('requests originating outside compose are rejected when they target it') is itself imprecise relative to tag.md and the dossiers and should eventually be narrowed to match -- but that is a doc-only fix outside this code-cluster row.

sources: dossier=tag, dossier=control-api (same as 104); doc=.ok-planner/design/concepts/tag.md:26; code=lib/control/controlapi/templates.go:195,288-295,331-333 handleDeployTemplate (validates via validTag only, no compose check)
note: Same reasoning as 104: the create-only compose-prefix reservation, corroborated by two independently-distilled intent dossiers plus tag.md, does not require a compose-origin check on the template-registration tag-upsert path either, since template registration with an existing tag name is functionally a tag move/create by an ordinarily-permissioned caller, not a foreign-client compose impersonation attempt.

sources: doc=.ok-planner/design/concepts/discovery-cache.md (exists, describes the cache structure/entry shape/reachability); code=lib/control/observability/discovery.go (Discovery, PeerEntry, Reachability -- no @concept annotation), lib/control/config/bundled.go:6 (only citing site)
note: Confirmed: `rg '@concept: discovery-cache'` matches only the peripheral bundled-registration populator, not discovery.go where the owned cache structure, per-service entry shape, and reachability status actually live. Per the project's own annotation convention ('annotate where the design is enforced or expressed'), this is a coverage gap on the owning site. Fix: add `// @concept: discovery-cache` to discovery.go at the Discovery/PeerEntry/Reachability definitions.

sources: dossier=cascade-graph('All cascade-graph HTTP handlers run inside a short fresh transaction (inTx). Read-only: no handler in this surface mutates state.' -- single artifact-tier source, 2026-05-11 log-convergence, dossier explicitly flags 'weigh accordingly'); code=lib/control/observability/handler.go:326-337 handleGetInstance (2 separate inTx calls), :328-472 handleGetNode (4 separate inTx calls: nodes, holdings, events, latest-run+attrs+summary)
note: Confirmed still present: handleGetNode splits one logical read across four separate transactions and handleGetInstance across two, so a run can settle between them, yielding a response whose events/holdings/summary describe different moments -- a real torn-read risk against the documented single-fresh-transaction invariant for this read-only observability surface. Provenance is single-source artifact-tier per the dossier's own caveat, but nothing in the record contradicts it and the invariant is internally coherent for an audit-facing dashboard. Fix: consolidate each handler's reads into one transaction.

sources: doc=.ok-planner/design/decisions/event-log-kind-enum.md ('Rimsky's app logic... consumes typed values exclusively... never raw strings'); dossier=event-log(Net position: 'Kinds are typed at the app boundary... app logic consumes typed values exclusively, never raw strings'); code=lib/foundation/auth/audit.go:14-20 (five raw string literals), lib/control/controlapi/audit.go:110-135 insertEvent (re-parses via events.ParseKindString, silently drops on mismatch)
note: Confirmed still present: auth/audit.go declares five wire-form string literals that duplicate events/kinds.go's operationalKindWireForm set with no compile-time or test-time link; a future rename of one side would silently drop the audit row (insertEvent logs and returns on ParseKindString failure) rather than fail loudly. The literals happen to match today, so no live bug fires, but this is exactly the kind of drift the cited decision was written to prevent. Fix: have auth/audit.go reference the typed events.Kind constants (or derive its string constants from them) instead of duplicating the wire-form literals.

sources: dossier=transition-reason(Net position, 2026-05-28 artifact ruling: instance_killed legal only from running/parked); doc=.ok-planner/design/concepts/transition-reason.md; doc=.ok-planner/design/concepts/node-run.md:59-61 (instance_killed legal from all five in-flight states); code=lib/foundation/cascade/state.go:68-121 NextState
note: Same underlying contradiction as row 807, viewed directly at the state-machine level: node-run.md and the current code agree (instance_killed legal from pending/stale/running/held/parked); transition-reason.md and the transition-reason dossier's 2026-05-28 ruling agree on a narrower running/parked-only set that predates the held state and the 2026-06-20 seven-state redesign. Neither the dossier nor the design corpus has explicitly reconciled the two docs since the redesign, so this needs a human ruling rather than a mechanical fix-code/fix-doc call. Same question as 807: widen transition-reason.md to match node-run.md/code, or narrow NextState (and node-run.md) to running/parked/held?

sources: doc=.ok-planner/design/concepts/blob-backend.md (exists); dossier=blob-backend(Required behaviors: memory-backend startup rejection unless unified, spill threshold, SweepOrphanedBlobs); code=lib/foundation/persistence/blob_config.go:68, lib/foundation/persistence/blob_spill.go, lib/runtime/orphan_blobs.go:26 -- none carry the annotation
note: Confirmed: `rg '@concept: blob-backend'` returns zero matches anywhere in lib/, cmd/, test/, tools/, even though concrete enforcement sites exist for the doc's stated invariants (the unified-only memory-backend gate, the spill-threshold check, the orphan sweep). Fix: add `// @concept: blob-backend` at these three enforcement sites.
